title: All Brakes Fail
front: Both the main brakes and emergency brake system are sensed to be inoperative.
back:
On-ground during taxi:
NOTE: Some brake pressure may still be available.
1. Wheel brakes and EMER Brake — Use if available to stop aircraft

title: Cabin Altitude
front: Cabin altitude above warning threshold and voice callout “CABIN ALTITUDE”.
back:
1. Crew oxygen masks — Don/100%/Establish COMM
2. Passenger oxygen — ON, Instruct passengers to don dropdown masks
IF rapid or explosive decompression:
3. Emergency Descent-3-NAE-02 — Accomplish

title: Cabin Pressure
front: Excessive positive or negative differential pressure.
back:
In Flight with excessive negative differential pressure:
1. Aircraft — Reduce descent rate

title: L ENG Fail / R ENG Fail
front: The indicated N1 has dropped 15% within 0.5 seconds. This will activate ATR during takeoff.
back: 1. Engine instruments — Monitor / Confirm

title: L Engine Fire / R Engine Fire
front: The indicated Engine Fire detector senses a temperature above 510 °C. Additional indications: Audio “Left Engine Fire” callout, RED “FIRE” light on the associated Engine Isolation Pushbutton, Synoptic page: FIRE flag on Engine ITT indication, Red color of associated engine outline.
back:
1. ENGINE FIRE — CONFIRM L or R
IF Fire Confirmed:
2. THRUST LEVER — IDLE
3. ENGINE SWITCH — OFF / STOP
4. ENGINE ISOLATION push button — PUSH
Check associated CAS “ENGINE ISOLATED” after five sec. CONFIRM ASSOCIATED green “1” illuminated.
NOTE: If possible, keep pitch and bank angles to within ±10° to achieve maximum extinguisher effectiveness.
IF CAS Message remains, affected side:
5. EXTINGUISHER push button — PUSH

title: ENGINE HUNG START ON GROUND
front: Indications: Engine Fails to Accelerate for > 30 Seconds.
back: 1. Engine Switch — OFF

title: ENGINE HOT START ON GROUND
front: Indications for Hot Start: Rapidly rising ITT approaching engine limits of 1,000 °C or ITT hanging between 900 °C and 1,000 °C for 15 seconds.
back: 1. Engine Switch — OFF

title: SWPS INADVERTENT PUSHER OPERATION
front: Non-commanded pusher operation, rapid nose-down motion.
back:
WARNING: NATURAL STALLS ARE NOT PREVENTED WITH THE STICK PUSHER INOPERATIVE. STALLS MUST BE AVOIDED WHEN THE STICK PUSHER IS INOPERATIVE.
1. Control wheel — Hold against pusher action
2. AP disconnect button — Press and hold continuously

title: ENGINE FIRE ON GROUND / TAIL PIPE FIRE
front: If during start, engine fire detector senses a temperature above 510 °C or else engine fire is indicated by ground personnel.
back:
1. THRUST LEVER — IDENTIFY/IDLE Affected Engine
2. ENG SWITCH — OFF
3. ENG ISOL pushbutton — Push/check after 5 sec amber ENG ISOL; Confirm green “1”
4. FIRE XTING pushbutton — Push to activate

title: ENGINE FIRE OR FAILURE DURING TAKEOFF
front: ENGINE FIRE OR FAILURE DURING TAKEOFF
back:
Airspeed below V1:
1. Rejected Takeoff - 3-NAE-19 — Accomplish
-END-
Airspeed at or above V1:
1. THRUST levers — Fully forward, ATR
2. VR — Rotate to 9° ANU Initially
3. Airspeed — Maintain at or above V2
4. L/G — When positive rate of climb – UP

title: REJECTED TAKEOFF
front: REJECTED TAKEOFF
back:
CAUTION: IF AUTOTHROTTLE WAS ENGAGED FOR TAKEOFF, ENSURE AUTOTHROTTLE IS DISCONNECTED BY EITHER PRESSING AN AT DISC PUSHBUTTON OR HOLDING THE THROTTLES AT IDLE FOR 2 TO 3 SECONDS UNTIL AUTOTHROTTLE DISCONNECTS.
1. THRUST levers — IDLE
2. BRAKES — Max Braking / As Required

title: EMERGENCY DESCENT
front: EMERGENCY DESCENT
back:
1. Crew Oxygen Masks — DON / 100% / Establish COMM
2. PASSENGER OXYGEN — ON, instruct passengers to don dropdown masks
3. SEAT BELTS — ON
4. THRUST Levers — IDLE
5. AIRBRAKE lever — OUT

title: SMOKE, FIRE, OR FUMES IN COCKPIT / CABIN
front: SMOKE, FIRE, OR FUMES IN COCKPIT / CABIN
back:
IMMEDIATE ACTION IF SMOKE AND / OR FUMES ARE PERCEPTIBLE:
1. CREW OXYGEN MASK — DON / select EMGCY / Vent valve open
2. Smoke Goggles — DON
3. Passenger OXYGEN — ON, Instruct PAX to don dropdown masks
LAND ASAP / INITIATE DIVERSION
4. Aircraft — Land as soon as possible

title: EMERGENCY EVACUATION
front: EMERGENCY EVACUATION
back:
1. PARK BRAKE — Set
2. ATC / distress message — Notify
3. ENG L+R switches — Both OFF

title: TCAS RESOLUTION ADVISORY
front: Accompanied by audio commands for climb, descend, level off or maintain vertical speed.
back:
1. Autopilot — Use yoke quick disconnect if AP engaged
2. Aircraft attitude — Immediately comply with RA commands indicated on the PFD
3. ATC — Inform of TCAS RA
When clear of conflict:
4. Aircraft — Return to previously assigned altitude and advise ATC

title: RH ENGINE START
front: RH ENGINE START
back:
RH Engine — Start
To start the RH Engine:
1. R Engine switch rotate to RUN
2. Confirm R Booster pump running and no FUEL PRESSURE CAS messages appear
3. R START Press

title: RH ENGINE START (CONTINUED)
front: RH ENGINE START (CONTINUED)
back:
1. Monitor start sequence as follows:
2. When pressing start button “START” will appear “ON” on the PFD
3. At about 10% N2, “START” and “IGN” is illuminated in inverse video. Check N1 is increasing
4. Observe light-up and engine parameters until “IDL” is reached
5. Depending on ambient conditions “START” and “IGN” extinguish at approximately 45% - 50% of N2

title: LH ENGINE START
front: LH ENGINE START
back:
1. LH Engine — Start
• Start LH Engine Accordingly
NOTE: The right engine must exit QPM and set to Ground Idle before Left Engine start

title: ENGINE APPROXIMATE GND IDLE VALUES
front: ENGINE APPROXIMATE GND IDLE VALUES
back:
N1: 25%
ITT: 400 °C
N2: Min 53.4%
FF: 160-180 lb
Confirm GEN 2 takes over and is supplying the aircraft.
NOTE: If TAT or reported OAT is <10 °C and visible signs of moisture are present then set the IPS rotary switch to AUTO/NAI.

title: AFCS ABNORMAL DISCONNECT
front: AFCS ABNORMAL DISCONNECT
back:
Indication: Flashing red “AP” on PFD and continuous “Cavalry Charge” aural warning.
1. Airplane control wheel — Grasp firmly and regain aircraft control
2. Autopilot Disengage switch — Press to cancel aural warning (pilot or copilot wheel)
3. Aircraft — Retrim manually as necessary
If no AFCS associated CAS messages:
4. Aircraft — Attempt to re-engage autopilot once

title: CLIMB
front: CLIMB
back:
1. Gear — UP
• Confirm Lever Up and Lights Out on System Summary Page
2. Yaw Damper — ON
• Confirm on FMA
3. Flaps — UP
• Confirm lever at 0 and indication on System Summary Page
4. Thrust — MCT
• Thrust Levers back to MCT gate within five min after setting T/O
• Verify MCT indications on both engine PFD indications

back:

2. MMO — 0.74 M

MMO schedule for maximum speed above 28,230 ft at this location.

title: QPM Operation — Engine Limits
front: Activation of QPM is permitted after at least two minutes of stabilized operation at ________ N2. After QPM termination, run engine at ground idle thrust for at least _____ before shutdown or increasing thrust.
back: Activation of QPM is permitted after at least two minutes of stabilized operation at Ground Idle N2. After QPM termination, run engine at ground idle thrust for at least 2 Minutes before shutdown or increasing thrust.

title: QPM Operation — Engine Limits
front: QPM operation is permitted provided the aircraft remains stationary with the ____ on. The thrust lever remains ____ during QPM operation. The maximum generator load while in QPM of ___ is not exceeded.
back: QPM operation is permitted provided the aircraft remains stationary with the Park Brake on. The thrust lever remains IDLE during QPM operation. The maximum generator load while in QPM of 250 A is not exceeded.

title: Engine Cooldown
front: Engine shut-down is permitted when the engine has been run at idle thrust for more than __.
back:
Engine shut-down is permitted when the engine has been run at idle thrust for more than 2 minutes.
NOTE
It is recommended that the engine bleed valve is closed during this time.

back: The autopilot (AP) and yaw damper (YD) must be OFF during takeoff and landing.

4. Coupled ILS approaches with G/S < 4.5° — 200 ft AGL

title: Yaw Damper Limits
front: Operation above ___ is prohibited with the Yaw Damper disengaged.
back: Operation above 30,000 feet MSL is prohibited with the Yaw Damper disengaged.

title: Severe Icing Conditions
front: Flight in freezing rain, freezing drizzle, or mixed icing conditions (supercooled liquid water and ice crystals) may result in ice build-up on protected surfaces exceeding the capability of the ___ ____ system, or may result in ice forming aft of the protected surfaces.
back: Flight in freezing rain, freezing drizzle, or mixed icing conditions (supercooled liquid water and ice crystals) may result in ice build-up on protected surfaces exceeding the capability of the Ice Protection system, or may result in ice forming aft of the protected surfaces.

title: Autopilot Usage in Icing Conditions
front: Care must be taken when using the autopilot that tactile cues, such as increased aileron forces, could potentially be masked by the autopilot function. Periodically ___ the autopilot to check for abnormal forces.
back: Care must be taken when using the autopilot that tactile cues, such as increased aileron forces, could potentially be masked by the autopilot function. Periodically disengage the autopilot to check for abnormal forces.

title: Nacelle Anti-Ice
front: The Nacelle Anti-ice (NAI) must be on for all ground operations, takeoff, and landing when:
back:
The Nacelle Anti-ice (NAI) must be on for all ground operations, takeoff, and landing when:
1. Visible moisture (i.e. standing water, slush, snow on taxi ways / runway) and indicated SAT or reported OAT <10 °C or
2. Ice or other frozen precipitation is observed adhering to any part of the engine inlet.

title: Nacelle Anti-Ice
front: The NAI must be on for climb, cruise, and descent when:
back:
The NAI must be on for climb, cruise, and descent when:
1. In visible moisture with TAT <10 °C, or
2. Flight through ice crystals, or
3. Anytime ice accumulation is observed on the airframe

title: Nacelle Anti-Ice
front: Do not operate the NAI when the TAT is ___ °C. Do not operate the NAI during ___ operation. When required for takeoff, NAI must be selected ON prior to setting ___.
back: Do not operate the NAI when the TAT is >10 °C. Do not operate the NAI during QPM operation. When required for takeoff, NAI must be selected ON prior to setting takeoff power.

title: Horizontal Stabilizer De-Ice (HSDI)
front:
Operation of the HSDI is not recommended when TAT < ___ unless required due to the presence of icing conditions.
If operated at TAT ≤ -40 °C, a ___ must be performed before takeoff.
back:
Operation of the HSDI is not recommended when TAT < -40 °C unless required due to the presence of icing conditions.
If operated at TAT ≤ -40 °C, a visual inspection of the pneumatic boots and a system functional test must be performed before takeoff.

title: Oxygen System Limits
front:

2. Minimum oxygen supply for each occupant for pressurized flight above 25,000 feet MSL — ?
back:
1. Minimum oxygen quantity for dispatch — 680 Liters
2. Minimum oxygen supply for each occupant for pressurized flight above 25,000 feet MSL — 10 minutes

title: Electronic Charts
front: Pilots are responsible for taxiing by ___ and for flying by airborne navigation with use of ___.
back: Pilots are responsible for taxiing by external visual references and for flying by airborne navigation with use of primary navigation instruments.

title: Electronic Charts
front: Position accuracy of a chart aircraft symbol can decrease in the case of insufficient ___ or ____. The aircraft symbol is not in-scale with ACE™ Electronic Charts.
back: Position accuracy of a chart aircraft symbol can decrease in the case of insufficient GPS signal reception or GPS sensor failure. The aircraft symbol is not in-scale with ACE™ Electronic Charts.

title: Electronic Charts
front: ACE™ Electronic Charts do not replace approved ____ or approved ____.
back: ACE™ Electronic Charts do not replace approved published papers or approved electronic systems for aeronautical charts.

title: Weather Radar
front: Operation of the weather radar is prohibited:
back:
Operation of the weather radar is prohibited:
1. Within a hangar or other enclosure
2. During airplane refueling/defueling operations
3. With personnel present within the acceptable safe distance and ± 60° from the aircraft nose

title: INAV Map
front:
1. The INAV topographical map shall not be used for primary ___.
2. The display of airspace shall not be used as the ___.
back:
1. The INAV topographical map shall not be used for primary navigation.
2. The display of airspace shall not be used as the sole airspace reference.

title: Smart View (SV)
front: Operations using Smart View are permitted when it is not used as a ___ of navigation reference or a ___ reference for obstacle clearance.
back: Operations using Smart View are permitted when it is not used as a primary source of navigation reference or a primary reference for obstacle clearance.

title: Vertical Situation Display
front: Use of the vertical situation display is permitted provided it is not used as a ___ of navigation.
back: Use of the vertical situation display is permitted provided it is not used as a primary source of navigation.

title: FMS
front: Accomplishment of ___ approach types using the FMS is prohibited.
back: Accomplishment of ILS, LOC, LOC-BC, LDA, SDF and MLS approach types using the FMS is prohibited.
